asr_text: The researchers also removed a description of a technique for throwing rocks to get more blocks from one AI's memory. After that, the average number of towers it could build fell. Its scores on other tasks did not change. At least for this AI, remembering that technique helped it build towers. One tip in the strategy notes was not something to overlook. Even so, it is too soon to wave a flag and say, play and get smarter, proof complete. But the fact that the experienced group did better and the fact that removing a particular memory lowered its score need to be looked at separately. These results alone do not show that play itself had an effect. Still, this changes how we see a detour. A discovery that is no use right now might become a useful card to play next time, if it is saved. If you see an AI jumping around on the island, pay attention to its notes as well as its feet. Its next tower might depend on a discovery written down in just one line.
